topic.title: your sibling's freedom
topic.claim: Your younger sibling's freedom was paid for with your arguments.
topic.moment: Your little sibling goes out past midnight with a shrug, no call, no fight, while you remember every battle it cost at that age.

turn.believed: Your younger sibling just has it easier because parents mellowed on their own.
turn.actually: They mellowed because you fought every rule first, and lost, so your sibling could win.

topic.because: You were the one who pushed the boundary, took the shouting, made your parents flinch and then reconsider. By the time it was your sibling's turn, the rule was already worn down. They inherited your scar tissue as freedom.
topic.payoff: Your sibling's easy life isn't luck. It's the ground you broke, taking the blows so they wouldn't have to.
topic.feeling: a wry tenderness for the version of you that fought and lost
topic.villain: the arrangement where the eldest spends the rule and the youngest spends it
topic.behaviour: eldest kids fight for permissions that younger siblings later get automatically
topic.mechanism: your battles wore down the rules, so the freedom your sibling enjoys was already paid for by you
topic.send_to: your own younger sibling, who should know what it cost
topic.why_now: holiday reunions that put the siblings in one house again
